events.outcome: Classic is an officially discontinued legacy tariff. Generic terms mention narrow indirect-channel legacy SIM activations but do not provide a current available channel; 2026 ordinary Big Bundles/Rolling plans are not Classic.

O2's current Classic page states top-up OR add a Bolt On OR chargeable activity at least once in any six calendar months; otherwise SIM disconnects and remaining credit is lost. Do not interpret six months as exactly 180 days or require £10 top-up every six months.
Current Classic standard UK text cost is 2p, call 3p/min, data 1p/MB; £0.04/year is not a validated total keep-alive cost, and UK domestic text tariffs do not establish overseas roaming SMS rates.
O2 online credit-card top-ups require a UK-bank card with UK-registered billing address, from £10 in pounds; vouchers/cash machine alternatives are not evidence of foreign signup funding.
O2 offers eSIM for eligible current PAYG and existing SIM swaps, but this is not evidence that a legacy Classic line is entitled to a Classic-specific eSIM exchange or offshore first activation.
General O2 PAYG Wi-Fi Calling exists but is currently unsupported outside the UK; do not present international Wi-Fi Calling as an OTP workaround.
Official O2 roaming pages do not verify Classic-specific China incoming SMS entitlement or exact bank/app OTP success; avoid blanket claims of free global incoming SMS.
One 2024 Classic customer reported disconnection despite claimed chargeable calls inside six months and required four support contacts to regain account access; anecdotal, not a line-loss percentage.
A self-described 2025 Classic holder reports continued 3p calling/2p SMS use and worries about 3G/2G device connectivity; the report establishes legacy active users, not new-sale availability.

A November-December 2025 O2 forum thread contains two existing Classic lines still shown as Classic and other users reporting account relabeling, auto-top-up loss and calls abroad failing; mixed tariffs, not proof Classic-wide roaming failure.

data.simType: Legacy physical; Classic-specific eSIM conversion eligibility unverified
data.acquisitionSummary: Classic Pay As You Go is an O2 legacy tariff unavailable for direct new-user selection or switches. O2's general 2023 terms allow rare indirect legacy-SIM activations, but no available verified Classic checkout/seller channel today. Do not treat current Big Bundles, Rolling Plan free SIMs or generic PAYG eSIMs as Classic acquisition.

keep.action: EXISTING CLASSIC HOLDERS ONLY: before every rolling six-calendar-month deadline, top up, add a Bolt On OR make a chargeable activity; 2p is the current domestic text charge, not a general roaming-SMS rate or guaranteed annual retention cost. Minimum £10 is a top-up funding denomination (UK-bank/UK-address card needed online), not a forced £10 every six months. A disconnected SIM loses remaining credit; reactivation/number recovery is not guaranteed. Maintain funded credit and confirm account state directly.

data.chinaActivation: No verified new-user Classic SIM issuance path. Generic O2 new PAYG SIM is activated by first top-up; an existing Classic SIM/eSIM may require an O2-network connection for replacement. China-first new activation and legacy eSIM abroad are unverified.
data.kyc: Generic UK PAYG signup is not presented as a postpaid credit-check flow. However, O2 may require security code, account confirmation or photographic ID for swaps/replacements; do not claim zero ID checks for all Classic operations.
data.payment: O2 says card top-ups require a UK-bank-issued debit/credit card registered at a UK address; only whole-pound top-ups from £10. Other official routes include vouchers and selected cash machines, availability abroad/unregistered foreign buyer unverified.
data.wifiCalling: O2 confirms general PAYG supports Wi-Fi Calling on suitable devices but says Wi-Fi Calling is NOT supported outside the UK. Classic-specific device/service eligibility and SMS over Wi-Fi are unverified; cannot treat as foreign OTP fallback.
data.roamingSms: O2's current PAYG roaming information covers European allowances and conditional non-European destinations, not proven Classic-specific attachment/SMS receipt in mainland China. No evidence here proves incoming Chinese roaming SMS free, continuity, or any bank/app OTP success; a 2p UK domestic text is NOT a Chinese roaming outgoing-text cost.
data.refund: O2 Classic says disconnection after more than six months without qualifying action loses the remaining credit; refund/recovery after deactivation not guaranteed.
data.holdReason: Classic is a legacy tariff unavailable to ordinary new customers. Indirect legacy SIM exceptions in terms do not establish a current purchasable route. Six-month inactivity criterion is known, but exact sustainable offshore cost, international payment, Classic eSIM eligibility and China SMS/OTP continuity lack evidence; known loss-of-number incident adds risk.
data.tariffSummary: Legacy-only: no verified current new-user purchase; existing-holder inactivity rule is any qualifying top-up/Bolt On/chargeable activity within six calendar months; UK domestic 2p/SMS; top-ups start £10, not every six months.
guideSteps: Existing Classic line only: check My O2 for the actual tariff and active status; do not mistake a Big Bundle or Rolling Plan SIM for Classic.

Before six calendar months elapse, perform and confirm one qualifying top-up, purchased Bolt On or chargeable activity. Make sure credit is usable; don't treat 2p UK domestic SMS as the cost of texting from abroad.
If maintaining abroad, check foreign attachment and roaming rates for the exact destination; Wi-Fi Calling isn't available outside the UK, and bank OTP reliability is not demonstrated.
Do not buy an ordinary O2 PAYG SIM expecting Classic; O2 no longer offers a general switch and unusual indirect-activation exceptions lack a verified acquisition path.
